newsitem.title: CHINA: Brokers bullish on China Eastern listing.
newsitem.headline: Brokers bullish on China Eastern listing.

text.p: China's third biggest carrier, China Eastern, looks set to become the first Chinese airline to be listed overseas and brokers are bullish despite worries about plane repayment costs and low domestic airfares.
Zhu Tonghai, a senior executive and deputy head of the firm's Communist Party branch, said China Eastern hoped the shares listed abroad would account for about 30 percent of total assets.
The timing of the listing depended on the company's preparations and conditions in the markets involved, he said in an interview on Tuesday.
Shen Yuankang, vice-minister of the General Administration of Civil Aviation of China, said on Monday the listing should go ahead by year-end in New York and Hong Kong.
"There is much work to do, on the use of land, valuation of assets, auditing of the balance sheets and agreement from the Bureau of Management of State Assets," Zhu said.
China Eastern's 1995 annual report put 1995 revenue at 7.0 billion yuan ($843 million) and profits at about 500 million.
In terms of number of planes, cargo and passenger volume, China Eastern ranks third in the country behind Air China and China Southern.
In 1995, China Eastern carried 6.57 million passengers and 176,000 tonnes of cargo, up from 5.61 million and 149,000 tonnes in 1994, its 1995 annual report said.
Brokers were positive about the listing prospects.

"Everyone expects the industry to have growth potential," said Alexandra Conroy, senior investment analyst with Barings Securities. "The infant industry has just been deregulated and there is lots of room for newcomers, such as China Eastern."
The airline, set up in 1988 with the division of the former national airline CAAC, had more than 60 planes flying 127 domestic and foreign routes, Zhu said.

"Compared to the second half of 1995, investors are more positive on China," Conroy said. "Most see 1997 as a stronger year for China, with a relaxation of credit, a cut in interest rates and stimulation of the economy.
"The listing should go well," she said. "It is a good concept. The degree of success depends on the price and penetration of the details."
An analyst at one foreign brokerage said foreign investors were optimistic about the growth of China's aviation industry and the fact that an airline was an easy company to understand.

Official figures released on Friday showed that passenger growth at Shanghai's Hongqiao airport, where China Eastern is based, grew an annual 23 percent from 1986 to 1990, reaching 11 million in 1995 and an estimated 13 million in 1996.
Official estimates put Shanghai's passenger volume in 2000 at 20 million. Work begins next month on a second international airport in the city's Pudong New Area.

Negative factors are cheap air tickets for domestic travellers, the company buying brand-new planes instead of serviceable second-hand ones and expensive aviation fuel, the foreign brokerage analyst said.
